dedupe_keys.name: remote sensing observations of source parameters and data integration at etna the respira database

description: Remote sEnsing obServations of source Parameters and data IntegRation at EtnA: the RESPIRA database is a data set described in a peer-reviewed Scientific Data article written by Luigi Mereu et al. Eruption Source Parameters (ESPs) are fundamental for quantifying paroxysm episodes and are essential inputs for volcanic ash dispersal models used to forecast tephra fallout and assess associated hazard. This is particularly crucial for densely populated regions like Mount Etna, Italy. Since 1986, approximately 150 Etna paroxysm episodes have been monitored using different sensors to estimate these ESPs. Coverage: national (IT); published in 2026. Formats: Excel, Image. The data are held in INGV and reached through its DOI listed on this page; the paper's Data Records section names it. Size stated by the repository: 8 columns indicating the parameters and 141 lines including the values for each event. Access is free of charge and open according to the article. The licence is Open Access, taken from DataCite rights of the deposit. Caveats: written from the Scientific Data article metadata (title, abstract, Data Records section) read on 2026-10-01; the data themselves were not opened or downloaded, so their contents, quality and current availability were not checked. It can support transport-network, traffic and mobility studies. Related records: none catalogued yet.
